extracted.intended_audience: Private-sector companies developing or operating Outer Continental Shelf (OCS) renewable energy leases and grants; lessees/grant holders; industry stakeholders; State, local, and tribal governments; and other entities submitting information on OCS renewable energy projects
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and procedural requirements in BOEM's proposed rule for OCS renewable energy activities, including inspection/self-inspection, reporting and recordkeeping, decommissioning, plan submission timing, and statutory/Executive Order compliance analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM inspections are optional but verify compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would update the regulations so that BOEM's conduct of an inspection of any OCS facilities and vessels engaged in activities under this subpart is optional. During inspections BOEM would verify that activities are conducted in compliance with the OCS Lands Act; the regulations in this part; the terms, conditions, and stipulations of the lease or grant; approved plans; and other applicable laws and regulations. BOEM would also determine whether proper safety equipment has been installed and is operating properly according to the SMS, as required in §585.810.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These revisions provide clarity and transparency to the BOEM inspections process and indicate that BOEM inspections serve to validate compliance with statutory, regulatory, lease, and plan requirements and the operation of safety equipment per the SMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM may conduct scheduled and unscheduled inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would clarify that BOEM may conduct both scheduled and unscheduled inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision provides greater flexibility for how BOEM conducts inspections; lessees should be prepared for both types of inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lessee obligations during BOEM inspections (access and records)
rubrics_metrics.description: For BOEM inspections, access for BOEM inspectors must be provided to all facilities and vessels used for activities authorized under this subpart. The proposed rule would also require that certain records be retained until BOEM releases the associated financial assurance and that the lessee make these records available to BOEM upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures availability of proper documentation during inspection; lessees should retain specified records until formal release of financial assurance and be ready to provide them upon BOEM request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-inspection frequency and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would require that you conduct an onsite inspection of each of your facilities at least once a year. The inspection must include, but is not limited to, all safety equipment designed to prevent or ameliorate fires, spillages, or other major accidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows BOEM to rely on the lessee's self-inspection to fulfill statutory annual onsite inspection requirements when BOEM does not inspect that facility. Lessee must maintain records and summarize results and provide them to BOEM upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and summary of self-inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would require that the lessee maintain records of the facility inspections, summarize the results of those inspections, and provide the records and result summaries to BOEM upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records and summarized findings should be preserved and organized to enable prompt BOEM review; these records support BOEM's ability to confirm compliance when BOEM relies on self-inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident reporting — oil spills cross-reference and BSEE reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would correct an erroneous cross-reference in paragraph (d) to provide the appropriate BSEE regulatory citation for reporting oil spills (BSEE 30 CFR 250.187).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oil spills must be reported as required by BSEE regulations; maintain familiarity with BSEE reporting procedures rather than relying solely on the BOEM citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decommissioning obligation for facilities and obstructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed subpart J contains requirements for decommissioning all facilities and obstructions on a lease, RUE, or ROW issued under BOEM's renewable energy regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessees/grant holders are responsible for decommissioning unless an explicit, limited exception applies (see met buoy/other Federal authority exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception when another Federal authority's decommissioning requirements apply (e.g., met buoys)
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited exception is proposed for facilities that are approved by, and subject to the decommissioning requirements of, another Federal authority. The proposed amendment is primarily intended to cover met buoys that would no longer require a SAP under proposed §585.600 and would be subject to the site clearance requirements in USACE's NWP 5, including removal within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a facility is covered by another Federal authority (e.g., USACE NWP 5), lessees may follow that authority's decommissioning requirements; noncompliance with USACE site clearance is addressed under USACE regulations (33 CFR part 326). BOEM retains authority to enforce decommissioning if the other authority does not require removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM authority to order earlier decommissioning ('idle iron')
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would allow BOEM to order decommissioning of facilities earlier than 2 years following lease termination if the facilities are no longer useful for operations. This mirrors the 'idle iron' authority found in the OCS oil and gas regulations at 30 CFR 250.1703.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM cites risks from idle facilities (environmental threats, hurricane damage, higher removal costs) and solicits comments on the meaning of 'no longer useful for operations' and whether it is the most appropriate standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for decommissioning applications under idle-iron authority
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes to add paragraph (e) to address the timing of decommissioning applications pursuant to the proposed 'idle iron' authority under §585.902.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow any new timing rules established for submitting decommissioning plans when BOEM exercises idle-iron authority; BOEM is proposing procedural changes to clarify timing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate Use RUE request information requirements and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would clarify the information requirements for an alternate use RUE and would broaden the alternate use RUE specifications to clarify that any OCS facility could be converted to an alternate use RUE (not only existing oil and gas facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide the clarified required information to request an Alternate Use RUE; the change expands applicability to additional facility types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for decommissioning facilities on an Alternate Use RUE
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would correct an outdated cross-reference in paragraph (b) addressing who is responsible for decommissioning an OCS facility located on an Alternate Use RUE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure understanding of the corrected citation to determine decommissioning responsibility for alternate-use facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA categorical exclusion determination
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM has concluded that this proposed rule falls under categorical exclusions established by DOI and BOEM, does not constitute a major Federal action significantly affecting the quality of the human environment, and does not require preparation of an environmental impact statement. BOEM has determined the proposed rule does not trigger any extraordinary circumstances that would require NEPA analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A final decision on NEPA analysis level will be made at the final rule stage; commenters may present arguments if they believe extraordinary circumstances exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act — OMB information collection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission to OMB for review under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 is required. BOEM will submit an IC request to OMB for review and approval and will request a new OMB control number (designated '1010-NEW'). BOEM may neither conduct nor sponsor, nor are respondents required to respond to, an information collection unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must obtain OMB approval before collecting information; BOEM plans to transfer burdens to an existing OMB control number after finalization. Stakeholders should be aware that BOEM cannot require responses absent a valid OMB number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Management System (SMS) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.810 clarifies that an SMS is required to conduct activities pursuant to a lease, from met buoy placement and site assessment work through decommissioning. A description of the SMS is required to be submitted for review by BOEM with a COP, and for review of a SAP or GAP if the facilities being installed are deemed by BOEM to be complex or significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A structured approach to safety is both expected and required for all lease-associated work; submit SMS descriptions with the applicable plan submissions as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual safety performance data reporting (Form BOEM-NEW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.812(b)(i) would require an annual summary of safety performance data covering the previous calendar year during which site assessment, construction, operations, or decommissioning activities occurred by submitting form BOEM-NEW, Performance Data Measures—Renewable Energy. This form would include company identification and number of injuries, illnesses, and hours worked by company employees and contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM will use these data to develop incident rates for benchmarking industry performance and to target regulatory and research programs; estimated burden is 82 hours × 10 submissions = 820 annual burden hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triennial SMS audit and corrective actions reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.812(b)(ii) would require a summary of the most recent SMS audit, corrective actions implemented or pending because of that audit, and an updated SMS description highlighting changes made since the last report. This report would be due every 3 years or upon BOEM's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides BOEM visibility into audit findings and remedial actions; BOEM estimates 75 annual burden hours for this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deeming periods and review-clock timing for FDR/FIR and verification reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.704 would allow BOEM 20-calendar days to deem the FDR and/or FIR submitted prior to commencing the 60-calendar day review time. Proposed §585.704 would also allow BOEM 20-calendar days to deem the project verification reports submitted prior to commencing the 30-calendar day review time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may use the 20-day deeming window to ensure completeness and identify deficiencies before the statutory review clock starts; applicants should expect an initial completeness check period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate FDRs and FIRs for major components and required integration statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.700(b) would allow separate FDRs and FIRs for major project components if an explanation is included in the reports describing how the systems comprising the project will function together effectively in an integrated manner in accordance with the project design basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting separate component reports, include an integration statement describing system interoperability and overall project design basis; BOEM solicits input regarding burden hours necessary to complete such statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow incremental funding of decommissioning accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed change to §585.529 would allow incremental funding of a decommissioning account under a BOEM-approved schedule during the operations period rather than requiring full funding before facility construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces upfront capital costs and enables investment in construction/operations; lessees must obtain BOEM approval for the funding schedule and remain compliant with financial assurance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Met buoys removed from BOEM SAP requirement (USACE NWP 5 governs)
rubrics_metrics.description: For site assessment activities, the proposed rule would remove met buoys from the reach of BOEM's regulations requiring submission of a SAP (§§585.600 through 585.618). Instead, a USACE NWP 5 permit would be the only Federal approval necessary to deploy a met buoy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM considers USACE permitting adequate to ensure safety and environmental responsibility; this change is intended to eliminate duplicative permitting and reduce costs/timelines for met buoy deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of detailed geotechnical survey reporting from COP to FDR/FIR
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would allow deferral of detailed geotechnical survey reporting from COP submission under existing §585.626(b) to FDR submission under proposed §585.701(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives lessees more time to complete surveys and reduces upfront costs; BOEM requests input regarding appropriate reallocation of geotechnical survey reporting hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced geotechnical core analysis sampling with BOEM approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would allow a lessee or a grant holder—subject to BOEM approval—to provide data from fewer than all facility foundation locations if they can demonstrate that the project area consists of generally uniform, predictable geophysical characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential cost savings by reducing the number of geotechnical investigations, provided the lessee can justify representativeness; BOEM estimated a 10 percent reduction in investigations for its analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act public comment solicitation on burden and minimization
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of BOEM's continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burdens, BOEM invites the public and other Federal agencies to comment on any aspect of the information collection, including necessity/usefulness, estimated burden hour increases/decreases, estimated non-hour costs, ways to enhance quality/clarity/usefulness, and methods to minimize respondents' burden (e.g., using automated or electronic technologies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should split cost estimates into capital/startup and annual operation/maintenance components and describe estimation methods, discount rates, and periods. Exclude certain costs (e.g., pre-1995 purchases) per PRA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) analysis and initial regulatory impact analysis (IRIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA requires agencies to prepare a regulatory flexibility impact analysis when a regulation will have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities. When issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking, the agency must describe the impact on small entities in its initial regulatory flexibility impact analysis. BOEM prepared an IRIA to quantify cost savings arising from this proposed rule and solicit public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM assessed affected entities (e.g., NAICS 221115 wind electric power generation) and concluded the rule likely does not have a significant adverse economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; nonetheless it prepared an IRIA and requests comments, including on impacts to small fishing businesses or small coastal communities if they believe they are affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act and Congressional Review Act determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM determined this proposed rule would not impose an unfunded Federal mandate on State, local, or tribal Governments, nor would it have significant or unique effects requiring a written statement under the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act. Given its economic implications (estimated annual economic effect of $100 million or more), the proposed rule is a 'major rule' under the Congressional Review Act and OMB guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must check statutory thresholds (e.g., $182 million single-year cost for Unfunded Mandates) and follow CRA procedural obligations; BOEM concluded thresholds are not triggered for unfunded mandates but the rule is major under CRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Orders compliance assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule includes required assessments under multiple Executive Orders: E.O. 12630 (takings implication — none required); E.O. 12866 and E.O. 13563 (regulatory planning and review — rule is a significant regulatory action; IRIA prepared); E.O. 12988 (civil justice reform — reviewed to eliminate technical errors and ambiguity); E.O. 13132 (federalism — no sufficient federalism implications); E.O. 13175 (tribal consultation — BOEM evaluated and concluded consultation not required at this stage but will consult on future actions when applicable); and E.O. 13211 (effects on nation's energy supply — not a significant energy action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking must document these EO analyses and determinations, quantify benefits/costs where required (e.g., IRIA under E.O.12866/13563), and follow EO-specific procedures for federalism, tribal consultation, takings, civil justice reform, and energy effects.
